sbh1.2:1.0: The avatārabhūmi opens by enumerating the six person-types it will define: *bhavya* (merely fit), the three grades of wholesome roots (mild, middle, strong), *niṣṭhā-prāyogika* (applied to the ultimate), and *niṣṭhā-gata* (arrived at the ultimate). Sections 1.4–1.27 define each in turn.
sbh1.2:1.9: *yāvat dṛṣṭi-ṛjū-kṛtā* — the Sanskrit *yāvat* signals 'as elaborated above, up to the point of ...'. Standard Buddhist-text shorthand: the full description from the *bhavya* entry above is implied, repeated in summary by the trailing milestone (here, 'making the view upright').
sbh1.2:1.18: *ātmabhāva-pratilambha* — 'attainment of [the final] individual existence.' Refers to the body-and-mind continuum that becomes the substrate for the path's culmination. The 'final' here means *carama-* (last in the saṁsāric series for this person), not chronologically late in life.
sbh1.2:1.26: *paramaśītī-bhāva-prāpta* — literally 'attained the supreme state of becoming-cool.' Coolness (*śīta*) is the standard Buddhist metaphor for nirvāṇa, contrasting with the burning of the kleśas. Rendered 'supreme calming' for English readability; 'supreme cooling' or 'highest peace' would also work.
sbh1.2:3.4: Restructured as a single question across 3.4–3.6 — the source uses three short *|*-separated clauses (asking about fixed measure, equal duration, and certainty respectively) that together form one question whose answer is given in 3.7. Punctuation here makes that visible.
sbh1.2:3.18: Sections 3.18–3.28 describe the descended person's distinctive *first mark* through a two-part contrast: 3.19–3.22 — rejection of an ill-stated dharma even when praised; 3.23 — simile for the un-descended state, where one cannot connect with even the well-stated dharma (like a honey-creature thrown into vinegar); 3.24–3.27 — the descended person's positive embrace of the well-stated dharma (like a honey-creature in honey). The contrast is the *mark* — what distinguishes the descended from the un-descended is precisely this changed orientation toward dharma.
sbh1.2:3.23: *svākhyātasya … dharmavinayasya* — 'of the well-stated dharma-vinaya.' Counterintuitive in context (the descended person is supposed to *embrace* the well-stated), but coherent if read as describing the *un-descended* state to which the simile compares: the un-descended person, like a honey-creature thrown into vinegar, cannot survive in the well-stated dharma until descent has occurred. 3.24 then turns to the post-descent positive case.
sbh1.2:8.3: *nihata-mada-māna-ahaṁkāra-guṇa-abhiniviṣṭa* — 'with conceit, pride, egotism, and quality-grasping struck down (*nihata*).' The descended person's afflictive impulses are subdued, not absent. *doṣa-dveṣṭā* (read as *a-doṣa, a-dveṣṭā* — 'free from defects, free from malice') closes the list.
